subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I need to produce a single TypeScript module for this vehicle model, keeping it decent despite limited effort. I'm thinking through the structure—since it's a static vehicle, joints may not be necessary, but I could add a simple turret joint and wheels to keep it reasonably detailed.

I'm setting up a riot control vehicle with chassis, turret, cannon, and wheel joints, sizing the body around 5.2m long and 2.3m tall with 0.5m wheels facing +Z. For the look, I'm planning a dark armored navy-black body with neon cyan/magenta accent lighting, plus decal textures for a corporate logo, hazard stripes, and a license plate, building the main hull shape by extruding a side-profile outline with a sloped windshield and cabin.

Now I'm working out the exact hull outline coordinates in the (z,y) plane, plotting points for the lower body, wheel arch area, hood slope, windshield rake, and roofline to form a closed, non-intersecting polygon before extruding it into the vehicle's hull shape.

Keeping the upper hull as is, I'm adding a slanted windshield using a thin rotated box spanning the cabin front.

Adding armored side window slits with dark cyan-tinted glass, then building roof lighting: a neon light bar split into magenta/cyan segments plus thin glowing strips running along the flanks for that cyberpunk aesthetic.

Now I'm adding a water cannon turret on the roof with a lathed base, housing, barrel, and glowing cyan nozzle ring aimed forward and slightly upward, plus a rear water tank with an "AQUA-" label texture.

I'm working out the positions of the roof turret, tank, and light bar so they don't overlap, then moving to the front end with a bumper push bar, grille with LED vents, and slim glowing headlight strips.

Still writing body details...

Setting up the wheel geometry now—tire cylinders with dark rubber material, hubcap discs textured with a neon spoke pattern, and joint positions for each of the four wheels at the corners of the chassis.

I'm thinking about the hull paint scheme next: a cyberpunk panelled armor look with rivets, countershaded dark navy fading lighter toward the top, and some grime weathering near the bottom edges.

Adding the magenta and cyan accent stripes near the top band, plus considering a stenciled "POLICE" text treatment on the sides.

I'm planning the rest of the texture set: glass, door logo, grille vents, wheel hub, tank label, rear plate/text, a roof marking "07", and rear doors with "CORPO ENFORCEMENT" lettering facing backward. Then I'm setting up the glow import from the kit's glow module.

Now I'm adding exterior hardware: an antenna with a neon tip, side mirrors with arms, roof spotlights, a camera dome, a searchlight, vertical red-magenta tail light bars at the rear corners, and a rear step bumper. I'm also sketching a hose from the water tank to the turret using a Catmull-Rom curve with a thin dark tube and ring bands along its path.

Setting up the joint hierarchy now: chassis as root, wheels and turret parented to it, a cannon joint on the turret aimed forward and slightly upward to give it an elevation angle.

Now I'm computing the barrel geometry, running a rod from the turret pivot out to the tip with a thicker shrouded section near the base, and planning a lathe nozzle piece at the muzzle end.

I'm defining a helper to create box parts with neon color constants and symmetric mirroring, then adding under-glow strips beneath the hull using magenta lighting near the bottom edge.

Now I'm adding side details—a thin cyan neon strip panel, small decorative chevrons and data-tick boxes along the sides, and a roof light bar made of alternating cyan and magenta segments.

Then I'm placing glowing headlights near the front slanted face, positioning them slightly forward and working out an angular slit shape using an extruded outline for a sharper look.

Now I'm sketching out the SVG textures: a glass texture with a dark gradient, cyan reflections, and HUD-style text, plus a transparent logo design.

Still writing SVG textures...

The tank cylinder runs along z-axis with faceted segments, positioned above and behind the turret with cradle straps made from thin torus rings wrapped around it. For end caps I'm considering hemisphere shapes attached to the cylinder ends.

For the license plate, I'm placing a small textured plane near the rear, but need to avoid overlapping it with the door decal texture - deciding to attach it to a separate rear bumper box instead, positioned low near the hull bottom.

For the wheel hub texture, I'm sketching neon cyan spokes radiating from a dark center circle. Then for the grille, I'm working out the angled front face geometry so the slotted magenta-glowing texture plane sits flush against the hull's slanted surface, calculating the normal direction from the face's tangent vector.

Positioning headlights...

Now I'm working out the bumper and skid plate geometry, extruding a wedge-shaped profile for the lower front fascia with hazard stripe coloring along it.

I'm also planning dark cabin window slits along the hull sides, positioning them relative to the roof's sloped profile so the windshield line and side windows align properly with the body curvature.

Adding mirrors as a small arm-and-box shape, and deciding to skip extras like ladders or roof-mounted sirens to keep things simple. I'll avoid importing unused modules like rng and make sure the paint function returns proper color types using mix, noise, smoothstep, and stripes from the SDK.

For the hull paint, I'm blending base panel colors with a darker tone near the bottom using noise for texture, then adding thin glowing pink and cyan stripe bands along the sides as accent details, keeping the color logic simple since I'll layer separate glow strips on top later.

Now I'm setting up a helper function to create box-shaped parts attached to the chassis bone with flat shading, plus a shorthand for applying glow effects, making sure the glow and paint color types stay compatible before moving into the wheel-building loop that positions wheels symmetrically on both sides.

Still writing wheel and chassis geometry...

Adjusting logo position to y 1.6 so it clears the window z-range without overlap. Now I'm checking the roof number plane placement, accounting for the slight roof slope between z -2.5 and 1.05 to compute the correct y-height at z 0.2 for the "07" marking.

I'm skipping the roof number entirely and instead defining a helper function rf(z) for the sloped roof height, then using it to position the turret base and tank cradle, with the tank center set roughly 0.36 above rf(-1.75).

Now I'm checking the barrel's reach forward—it rises clear over the roof light bar near z 0.75, so I'm placing the light bar housing and glowing segments just above the roof slope there. I'm also sketching out a decal placement for the tank label, positioned on the side of the faceted twelve-segment tank.

Adding a pressure gauge texture to the turret housing's side plane, then setting up the cannon rod geometry by computing direction vectors between two points along the barrel's trajectory.

Still writing barrel geometry...

Now adding rings and torus details at intervals along the barrel, plus small water-jet pipe rods, and defining the turret housing's box and base cylinder dimensions along with a top sensor cube.
